info.title: OpenBooks API
info.summary: PotatoStack patched build of evan-buss/openbooks: IRC Highway eBook search and download, plus a REST API
info.description: PotatoStack v5 of evan-buss/openbooks (upstream base v4.5.0). Adds bearer-token authentication on every API route, a REST API (/api/v1) on top of the websocket-only upstream app, path-traversal hardening on all library endpoints, loopback-only bind by default, TLS verification for IRC, and vulnerability fixes in the dependency tree. All /api/v1 and legacy endpoints require a token when the server was started with OPENBOOKS_TOKEN (Authorization: Bearer header, X-OpenBooks-Token header, or ?token= query parameter). Only the static SPA and this document are unauthenticated. v5.1.2 adds GET /api/v1/downloads (book completions recorded by the api session) and GET /api/v1/metrics (Prometheus text format), and the api IRC session now re-establishes itself after the reader detects a dead connection. v5.2.0 adds the persistent Wanted watchlist (POST/GET/DELETE /api/v1/wanted with a re-search poller), the Atom feed of library activity (GET /api/v1/feeds/atom), the OPDS 1.0 catalog of the local library (GET /opds, with ?search=), and the unified multi-source search (POST /api/v1/search/unified, IRC + Prowlarr with per-source status). v5.3.0 adds scoped bearer tokens (OPENBOOKS_SCOPED_TOKENS; ui/search/newznab/admin, a scope miss is a 403), a TTL search-result cache (GET/POST /api/v1/search-cache[/clean]), quality-control filters on search and the wanted watchlist (formats/language/maxSizeBytes/prefer), cross-source result dedupe (dedupKey grouping in /search/unified), per-job download tracking with retry (GET /api/v1/jobs, POST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/retry), sha256 verification of a landed book (POST /api/v1/verify), wanted-entry failed-release tracking with backoff/stale (GET /api/v1/wanted entries now carry attempts/seenReleases/staleSince), and the ebook sidecar flag (withSidecar on POST /wanted).

servers.description: The openbooks base path (e.g. http://host:8083/ or http://host:8083/openbooks/)

get.summary: Server health and version; the UI uses this as its token probe

get.description: Requires the server to run with --persist. Returns files in the books directory (dotfiles and *.temp staging files excluded). Subdirectories are listed as flat entries; use the download endpoint with the subdirectory prefix to fetch files inside them.

404.description: Persist mode is off or the library is unavailable

get.description: The name may contain percent-encoded subfolder prefixes (the bookdl pipeline organizes into subfolders). Every path component is validated to stay inside the books directory.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: File name, optionally with subdirectory prefix, URL-encoded

404.description: Persist mode off or file not found

delete.description: Only a single top-level entry can be deleted (same hardening as the upstream endpoint). Subdirectory content is not exposed to DELETE.

post.description: Sends the query to the IRC search bot and, by default, blocks until the parsed results arrive (120 s timeout). The first call opens the shared server-side IRC session; subsequent searches are rate limited to the configured search interval (default 10 s) with 429. Results are parsed book rows; the `full` field is the `!`-prefixed identifier to hand to /api/v1/download.

409.description: Another search is already in flight

429.description: Rate limited (search interval). The Retry-After header carries the seconds to wait before the next search.

502.description: Could not connect to the IRC server

post.summary: Request a book download over DCC
post.description: Asks the IRC book server to send the file to openbooks. The file lands in the books directory (it may take a while - DCC transfer speed). Poll GET /api/v1/library until the new file appears.

callback.description: Present (informational) when a callbackUrl was accepted.

502.description: Could not connect to the IRC server

get.description: The download directory and persistence flag in effect for this running instance.

put.description: Change the download directory and/or persistence flag without a restart. The new directory must be absolute, existing or creatable, and writable; a rejected change leaves the settings untouched.

400.description: Invalid body or rejected download dir

get.summary: Newznab search endpoint (openbooks as a book indexer)
get.description: The standard Newznab protocol so Prowlarr and Readarr can add openbooks as a book indexer. Auth is the same token as the REST API, carried the Newznab way (?apikey=*** Bearer / X-OpenBooks-Token / ?token=*** also accepted. t=search reuses the same IRC session, rate limit and single in-flight rule as POST /api/v1/search. Download URLs in the items point at GET /api/v1/library/{name} - callers add ?token=*** to fetch the file.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Book title or author (required for t=search)

parameters.name: apikey
parameters.description: The openbooks token, Newznab form. Any of the accepted token forms works.

409.description: A search is already in flight on the shared api session

429.description: Rate limited (shared with POST /api/v1/search). The Retry-After header carries the seconds to wait; Prowlarr/Readarr back off on it.

502.description: Could not connect to the IRC server

get.description: Reports which peer integrations (Prowlarr, Audiobookshelf, Calibre-Web, Readarr) are configured and whether a download-completion webhook is set. With ?probe=1 each configured peer is probed with a cheap GET and reported reachable/unreachable with a short reason. Use this after a peer container recreate: bridge IPs on 172.22.0.0/16 are dynamic and a recreate can move a peer's IP, in which case the probe reports unreachable until the OPENBOOKS_*_URL env value is updated.

parameters.name: probe
parameters.description: Run a live reachability probe against each configured peer

get.summary: Book completions recorded by the api session, oldest last
get.description: The completion map the api session fills as books land over DCC. The polling path for POST /api/v1/download callers without a callbackUrl: before v5.1.2 learning that a file landed required diffing GET /api/v1/library.

200.description: The completions (an empty array when none)

404.description: Persist mode is off (same contract as /api/v1/library)

get.summary: Prometheus text-format metrics: openbooks_up, openbooks_version, openbooks_irc_connected, session/search/download counters, the completion gauge, the callback queue size, and openbooks_http_requests_total{status}

post.summary: Add a book to the Wanted watchlist
post.description: The re-search poller (OPENBOOKS_WANTED_POLL_INTERVAL, default 5m) sends one IRC search per tick until the entry matches. Duplicate queries (case-insensitive) are a 409. Token-gated like every /api/v1 route.

409.description: A wanted entry with the same query already exists.

delete.summary: Remove a book from the Wanted watchlist

get.description: Atom 0.3 feed: one entry per book the api session has seen - the current library contents (persist mode, newest first) plus the recent completions from GET /api/v1/downloads. Capped at 100 entries. No downloader-shaped comparable project ships such a feed; it is the zero-polling integration point for the rest of the stack.

post.summary: Search all configured sources in one request
post.description: Searches the IRC session and Prowlarr (both by default; restrict with sources) and returns one normalized result list with a per-source status. The IRC leg is subject to the shared 10s rate limit and single-flight rule: a 429/409 there is reported in the source status, not as a failed request.

200.description: The normalized results and per-source statuses.

400.description: Missing query or unknown source name.

get.summary: OPDS 1.0 catalog of the local library
get.description: Serves the library directory tree as an OPDS 1.0 acquisition feed (newest first, 500-entry cap, hidden files and .temp excluded). ?search=term is a case-insensitive title filter (the OPDS search contract). Entry links are absolute and carry ?token=*** - OPDS clients cannot set Authorization headers on content fetches. 404 when persist mode is off.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring filter on the file name.

404.description: Persist mode off, or the library is unavailable.

get.summary: Per-job download status (in-flight and terminal, newest first, 256-entry cap)
get.description: Every download requested through POST /download is tracked as a job: the request identifier, the book it resolved to, the current status (requested/downloading/completed/failed), and the file name and sha256 on completion. The map is capped at the 256 most recent jobs; older ones fall off silently (GET /api/v1/downloads is the durable completion record).

403.description: Token is valid but lacks the required scope.

post.description: Sends the job's original download command to the IRC session again. A job whose status is not failed returns 409 (re-fetching a completed job is the verify/re-download path, not a retry). The job status resets to requested and its id is preserved.

403.description: Token is valid but lacks the admin scope.

409.description: Job is not in a retryable state.

post.summary: sha256 verification of a landed book
post.description: Computes the sha256 of a file in the download directory and compares it to the hash recorded when the job completed. {file} is required; {jobId} is optional (without it the hash is recorded as a baseline for a later verify). status is ok (hash matches / newly recorded), mismatch, or missing (file not found).

400.description: Missing or invalid body / file name.

403.description: Token is valid but lacks the admin scope.

get.description: The v5.3.0 TTL cache in front of performSearch: current entry count, hit/miss counters, the configured TTL, and a bounded sample of cached query keys. POST /api/v1/search is the consumer: an exact hit (same query, same quality filters) inside the TTL is served with zero IRC traffic and carries note=cached.

403.description: Token is valid but lacks the required scope.

post.description: Drops every cached entry (hit/miss counters are preserved). Use after a large library change when the cached answers are stale but you do not want to restart.

403.description: Token is valid but lacks the admin scope.

openbooksToken.description: The openbooks token, accepted as Authorization: Bearer *** X-OpenBooks-Token header, ?token=*** or the Newznab ?apikey=*** query form (indexer tools such as Prowlarr/Readarr append apikey to the indexer URL). Constant-time compare. No token configured = unauthenticated single-user mode (upstream behavior).

ircConnected.description: Whether the shared api IRC session is up. Self-healing: the session re-establishes lazily on the next search, so false after a drop is transient.

wait.description: Block until results arrive (default). false = fire and forget.

note.description: Set on timeout or no results

book.description: The !-prefixed identifier from the search results

callbackUrl.description: Optional. When set, openbooks POSTs a JSON body {status,book,file} to this URL once the requested book has landed. http(s) only. The api session processes book DCC transfers in request order, so completions are paired with requests FIFO. One retry; a dead URL is logged and dropped.

downloadDir.description: Directory where downloads are saved; the library lives in downloadDir/books.

persist.description: Keep books after sending them to the client. When false, a served book is deleted afterwards.

SettingsUpdate.description: Partial update: only the provided fields are changed.

WantedItem.description: One entry of the persistent Wanted watchlist. A wanted entry is re-searched through the shared api IRC session on the poller interval until it matches; autoFetch entries are fetched automatically on the first match.

fetchedAt.description: Set when an auto-fetch was sent.

matchedAt.description: Set when the poller found results.

matched.description: The last search results the poller matched this entry against.

UnifiedResult.description: One normalized hit from any source. The Prowlarr leg is a release (url); the IRC leg is a DCC book identifier (bookId, fetched via POST /api/v1/download).

UnifiedSourceStatus.description: The per-source outcome of a unified search. One dead source never hides the others' results.

hits.description: How many results this source contributed.
